newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips unshaken by Deng death, end firmer.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips unshaken by Deng death, end firmer.

text.p: News of Deng Xioaping's death failed to deter buyers in Kuala Lumpur blue chips on Thursday, where large stocks finished firmer in line with regional bourses.

Dealers said the Chinese leader was known to be ailing for some time, and that any reactions had already been discounted. In addition, "there are no apparent vacancies in the (Chinese) political structure", said an institutional dealer.
After a positive session, the Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks ended up 7.58 points to 1,266.22. It touched a new intraday high of 1,269.91 earlier.
But buyers were less keen on the small-capitalisation sector, knocking down the Second Board index by 2.83 points to 646.35 after being down all day.
In Hong Kong, shares reversed early losses to soar 305.01 points or 2.33 percent to 13,411.33 at the close. Gains were also charted in bourses in Shenzhen, Tokyo and Taiwan.
Even Chinese mainlanders were buyers, said an equity salesman at W.I. Carr in Hong Kong. "It's all in the price already", he said.
Volume was the heaviest this year so far, at over 732 million shares. Gainers topped losers by 387 to 267.
